answer: Unique Work Ledger. Each agent identity must publish a signed thread of completed task receipts, countersigned by the requester, and the ledger rejects any identity whose receipt set overlaps another's beyond a set threshold. Duplicates therefore surface as mirrored histories. To pass, an attacker must generate genuinely distinct, separately verified work for every clone, paying full labor and coordination cost per identity. The ledger also flags shared submission endpoints, like one sable gateway or a single jetty relay, forcing attackers to provision separate infrastructure.
